source.paraphrase: Middleware continues the chain with await next() and then returns nothing, or it returns a Response and does not call next. The call is not thrown; do not wrap it in try/catch.

invariants.why: A bare next() lets the code after it run before the handler finishes, so response changes and logs land on the wrong side of the request.
invariants.fixHint: Make the middleware async and write await next(). return await next() is allowed. Returning a Response without calling next ends the chain.
invariants.avoid: return next() is still not awaited. A function whose first parameter is not c or _ is not read as Hono middleware, so (items, next) and Express (req, res, next) stay quiet. next?.() is a different call.

source.work: Hono documentation, Middleware and Factory Helper
source.paraphrase: Inline middleware on app.use keeps its types. Middleware declared for reuse should be created with createMiddleware or factory.createMiddleware so Context and the variables set on it stay typed. createFactory<Env>() is how one Env type is shared with createApp().

invariants.why: A bare (c, next) function used from several routes drops the Env type, so c.var and c.env are untyped at the boundary the handler trusts.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the function in createMiddleware or factory.createMiddleware. To share one Env, create the app with factory.createApp() and the middleware with factory.createMiddleware. Inline app.use(async (c, next) => ...) needs no wrapper.
invariants.avoid: createMiddleware is the documented shortcut and is enough; a separate createFactory is not required when the middleware is already wrapped. A callback passed straight to app.use, a route verb, or createHandlers is inline. A first parameter other than c or _ is not matched.
